citeAs: Bian, Yuxuan, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, and Qiang Xu (2025). Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation. arXiv.
creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (ByteDance; The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
description: VAP-Data is a semantic-controlled paired video generation dataset introduced with Video-As-Prompt. It contains over 100K curated paired video samples across 100 semantic conditions spanning concept, style, motion, and camera categories, built to support unified semantic-controlled video generation.
name: VAP-Data
rai:dataBiases: The paper states that VAP-Data is synthetic and derived from other generative models, so it may inherit the specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates. It also notes that semantic conditions are relatively limited and synthetic, and that performance depends on caption quality and structural similarity between subjects.
rai:dataCollection: The authors curated thousands of high-quality real reference images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. They then used image-to-video visual-effects templates from commercial models such as VIDU and Kling, together with community LoRAs, to create paired videos by matching each image to compatible templates, yielding over 100K paired samples across 100 semantic conditions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of thousands of high-quality real images curated from the Internet, plus visual-effects templates and outputs from commercial models and community LoRAs used to bootstrap paired videos.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that VAP-Data is synthetic, relatively limited in semantic conditions, and derived from other generative models, so it may inherit source-template biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations. It also states that inaccurate semantic descriptions or large subject mismatch can degrade generation quality, and that broader real-world data collection is left to future work.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After curating reference images, the authors matched each image to all compatible visual-effects templates from commercial models and community LoRAs to generate paired videos. They also evenly sampled 24 semantic conditions from four categories with 2 samples each for the test subset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The paper describes curating high-quality reference images and matching each image only to compatible templates, since some templates restrict subject categories. It also reorganizes the resulting dataset into four primary categories—concept, style, motion, and camera—with detailed subset distributions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The ethics statement says the dataset/model are intended for research, education, and creative prototyping, and not for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments. It identifies misuse risks including identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and sexualized or violent media, and proposes mitigations such as a research-only release, acceptable-use policy, and default content filters.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to support research on unified semantic-controlled video generation across concept, style, motion, and camera conditions, and downstream applications such as transferring semantics from reference videos to new subjects, handling different reference videos with the same or different semantics, and fine-grained prompt-based video editing.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial image-to-video models and templates from VIDU and Kling, community LoRAs, and model-based evaluation tools Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5 are described in the dataset creation/evaluation pipeline.
